CashBridge
How a case runs Two portals Measured trust

For export SMEs and the banks that fund them

Know the week your cash runs out. Bridge it with evidence a bank can check.

CashBridge reads your bank feed, invoices and shipping documents, forecasts 13 weeks of cash, prices every way to cover the gap, and drafts a funding pack. Your Director approves it with a one-time code; your lender re-verifies every hash.

All companies, people, lenders and bank feeds in this demo are synthetic or mocked.

How a case runs

One loop, five steps. The agent does the reading and arithmetic; people make the two decisions that matter.

  1. Agent

    Anticipate

    Forecasts 13 weeks from open invoices, deposits and payroll, and names what causes the first negative week.

  2. Agent

    Prove

    Matches bank credits to invoices, checks each invoice against its purchase order and bill of lading, and blocks lookalike-domain payment emails.

  3. Agent

    Compare

    Prices factoring, a bridge loan and early-payment discounts as a true annual cost, then stress-tests the choice week by week.

  4. Director

    Approve

    Reviews the pack the accountant prepared and releases it with a one-time code bound to that exact pack. The preparer cannot approve.

  5. Lender

    Verify

    Sees only what was released, recomputes every document hash and the audit chain, and records the credit decision.

Two portals, one evidence trail

Each side signs in separately. Permissions are enforced by the server, so hiding a button grants nothing.

SME workspace

Chief accountant prepares. Director approves.

  • Run the Autopilot from cash gap to a drafted funding pack
  • See every figure tagged verified, calculated, estimated, assumed or missing
  • Test what-ifs: slower buyers, smaller deposits, FX moves
  • See how often a plan survives 2,000 simulated quarters, and which plan the Intelligence Core would pick
  • Review contracts, bids, budgets and green-investment evidence
  • The agent cannot submit a pack or move money
  • The person who prepares a pack cannot approve it

Bank review

Credit reviewer at the partner lender.

  • Receive packs only after the SME Director releases them
  • Recompute document, bundle and approval hashes independently
  • Read the agent's reasoning, its assumptions and what it could not check
  • Approve, decline or request information, with the decision logged
  • No access to the SME's inbox, contacts or unreleased drafts
  • No automated credit decision: a named person decides

Trust you can measure

Run make trust to reproduce these numbers. They come from the same code that serves this page.

25/25adversarial requests refused or detected: forged sessions, self-approval, replayed codes, double financing, tampered documents, prompt injection
5/5Autopilot scenarios end correctly, including the ones where the right move is to stop or hand over to a person
0.091 vs 0.146Brier score of the buyer payment model against the historical-rate baseline, walk-forward on 167 synthetic invoices: synthetic data, indicative only

Working in this demo

Forecast, matching, APR, coverage and stress engines; OTP-bound approval; hash-chained audit log and invoice registry; server-side roles for both portals.

Mocked

Bank feeds, the lender connector and its price list, buyer KYC. The data set is synthetic.

Not claimed

Cross-lender duplicate checks, production identity management, legal review of contracts, credit approval, green taxonomy certification.
